source_issues.issue: echo $SHELL reports the configured shell environment value rather than reliably identifying the shell currently executing. The source claim is faithfully preserved.
The blanket statement that all course commands work in both bash and zsh lacks qualifications for shell options and platform/tool availability. Translation preserves its scope.
The protected grep loss | wc -l example counts matching lines, not all occurrences; a line may contain multiple matches. Comment retained exactly.
The source says three redirects but lists five rows, including a pipe operator. Chinese correctly preserves 三种 instead of silently changing the source count.

Terminal-close survival table is categorical and nohup protection is specifically against the hangup signal, not every way a process can terminate. The translation retains 挂断信号 and makes no broader immunity claim than the source.

kill and pkill patterns may match multiple processes; termination is signal-based, F9 opens the signal action, and commands do not establish safe targeting or guaranteed graceful termination. Protected code and equivalent prose preserved.
Sorting processes by memory use cannot alone establish a memory leak; the source oversimplification remains in translation.
Sourcing the alias script via a repository-relative path from startup configuration assumes a suitable working directory. Path left unchanged.

The mail pipeline assumes configured mail tooling and notifies after pipeline completion without proving training succeeded; xargs examples do not protect whitespace-containing filenames; diff command is not actually a side-by-side view; the Hugging Face URL is illustrative. All examples were preserved and not executed.
A Bash process started with SHELL=/bin/sh reported SHELL=/bin/sh and BASH_VERSION=5.2.37(1)-release, demonstrating that the variable does not identify the currently executing shell reliably
